mission: LÉLU 2.1 — geometry fidelity and mathematical validation
observed: Two attempts to stop strands crossing her face failed before the shipped one: deflecting strands produced a cage of horizontal rods; cutting at the voxel plane left 574 of 1350 strands, i.e. most of the hair.
studied: Where a strand actually crosses the face, and what a cut removes along the strand's arc length.
question: How do you keep hair off the face without deleting most of it?
hypothesis: Cutting every strand at the boundary of the hair field box is sufficient.
method: Keep the root set and the curl law fixed; change only the cut predicate. Compare the number of surviving strands and inspect a front render.
results: Voxel-plane cut: 574/1350 strands survived and the crown went bald. The shipped predicate cuts at the face plane (z > head[2] + 0.03) after the curl is generated, which keeps the face clear and the crown covered.

evidence.note: sweepTube — the geometry the cut applies to

learned: A cut plane chosen for the volume grid is not a cut plane chosen for the body. The failure was not the idea of cutting, it was cutting along the wrong surface.
limitations: The 574/1350 count came from an intermediate build whose artefact was not preserved; the shipped behaviour is reproducible, the failed count is quoted from the session record.
The deflection attempt was rejected visually; no metric was defined for it.
applications: Any strand-level culling must be measured in surviving strands before it is accepted.
Volume boundaries and anatomical boundaries are different predicates.
nextQuestions: What fraction of strands does the shipped face-plane cut remove, and where?
Can the cut be replaced by a length-preserving bend so roots keep their length?

assumptions.statement: the hair field box boundary is a good enough face cut
deflecting strands sideways is visually acceptable
